Every MYP unit is set in one of six contexts: identities and relationships; orientation in space and time; personal and cultural expression; scientific and technical innovation; globalization and sustainability; fairness and development.
Five groups of skills you practise in every subject: thinking, communication, social, self-management and research. Teachers name them in each unit.
Ten traits the IB hopes you grow into: inquirer, knowledgeable, thinker, communicator, principled, open-minded, caring, risk-taker, balanced and reflective.
Each subject has four criteria (A, B, C and D), each marked from 0 to 8. Your teacher tells you which criteria a task is assessing before you start.
Each unit starts from one sentence that links a big idea to a global context. Reading it tells you what the unit is really about.
The MYP asks you to take action in your community: helping, campaigning or volunteering, and then reflecting on what you learned.
The MYP brings two subjects together in at least one unit every year, so you use both to understand one problem.
In Design you go through four stages: inquiring and analysing, developing ideas, creating the solution, and evaluating.
Many criteria ask you to reflect: what worked, what did not, and what you would change. It is marked, not just a nice extra.
